name: W1 — Research over a local corpus (NO internet)

assignments.name: question
assignments.value: How does retrieval-augmented generation find the right chunk of a document?

nodes.name: Synthetic question
nodes.notes: THE QUESTION LIVES HERE, not in the caller. FOUND BY QA (NOM-302): the first version wired an empty manual trigger straight into the embedding request, so the demo embedded `undefined` and retrieved whatever that happens to be near. A demo with no input is not a demo. `samples setup` records this exact string in w1_expected alongside the corpus file the harness asserts comes back first, so the question and its assertion cannot drift apart.

nodes.name: Embed the question
nodes.notes: LiteLLM REQUIRES A KEY AND ALWAYS DID. MEASURED (NOM-302): an unauthenticated POST here returns 401, so the first version of this template could not have completed even with weights loaded and tables present. The credential carries a LiteLLM VIRTUAL key minted by `samples setup` with its own budget — not the master key, which would have no spend ceiling and no way to revoke this demo alone.

parameters.query: SELECT source, content, embedding <-> $1::vector AS distance FROM w2_chunks ORDER BY embedding <-> $1::vector LIMIT 5

nodes.name: Nearest chunks (pgvector)
nodes.notes:
THE CORPUS IS LOCAL AND PRELOADED. This demo needs no internet and gets none: Open WebUI's web search is off in every profile and there is no web-search group in this release. The internet-backed version of this demo is a LATER release, not a setting.

The $1 placeholder is bound through Query Parameters. FOUND BY QA (NOM-302): the first version wrote $1 into the SQL and supplied nothing, so Postgres rejected the statement before pgvector was ever reached. `distance` is selected so the harness can assert the ORDER BY actually ran rather than trusting row order.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'local-chat', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Answer using ONLY this context. Cite the source of each claim.\n\n' + JSON.stringify($input.all().map(i => ({ source: i.json.source, content: i.json.content }))) }], max_tokens: 160 }) }}

nodes.name: Answer with citations
nodes.notes: The `distance` column is dropped from the prompt on purpose: a float in the context is a token the model will try to explain.

parameters.query: INSERT INTO w1_runs (question, top_source, sources, distances, answer) VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, $4::jsonb, $5) RETURNING run_id, top_source, created_at

nodes.name: Record the run (answer + citations)
nodes.notes: THE DEMO WRITES ITS OWN EVIDENCE. `aistack samples run W1` asserts against this row rather than against the CLI's stdout, for two reasons: stdout shape is an n8n implementation detail that changes between minor versions, and a run a human did in the UI leaves the same evidence as a run the harness did. An answer stored next to the sources it cited is also the only form in which a citation claim can be re-checked later.
